candidate.title: TIVA
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina schematic of Transcriptome In Vivo Analysis (TIVA): caged-tag entry into live cells, CPP release, selective photoactivation, poly(A) mRNA capture, streptavidin affinity recovery and the mRNA endpoint. Downstream cDNA library preparation and RNA sequencing are described in text but are not depicted operations. The target is the captured polyadenylated transcript population of the selected cell, whose spatial association is established by localized activation.

states.label: Caged TIVA-tag before cell entry
features: Biotin-bearing U-rich capture segment paired with A-rich blocking segments; two PL labels denote photocleavable linkers.
Primary paper resolves the generic U/A symbols as a poly-2′-deoxy-2′-fluorouridine capture segment and two poly-2′-O-methyladenosine blocking segments in a caged hairpin.
Cy3 and Cy5 fluorophores; CPP is attached through the depicted S-S disulfide.
Biotin is an attachment on the capture oligonucleotide; mRNA acquires biotin-mediated affinity by hybridizing to that oligonucleotide.

operations.label: Photoactivate
operations.description: Light cleaves the two PLs; the blocking fragments dissociate and the U-rich mRNA-binding segment becomes accessible.
operations.mechanism: Selective laser photoactivation cleaves the two PLs of the caged hairpin. The resulting shorter modified A-rich blocking fragments dissociate, exposing the modified U-rich capture oligo.
operations.information_effect: Activation identifies the cell in which capture can occur. Cy3/Cy5 are a loading/uncaging FRET reporter; they are not transcript identifiers.
